key_insight: Combining Knowledge Graphs with Large Language Models structures domain knowledge and ML outputs so explanations become context-aware and easier for manufacturing users to understand.
problem_solved: Opaque ML explanations and the gap between domain expertise and model outputs make it hard for manufacturing stakeholders to trust, debug, and act on ML predictions.
method: Construct a Knowledge Graph that stores domain-specific entities, ML model results, and their linked explanations to create structured, queryable context.
Use Large Language Models to interpret KG contents and generate concise, user-friendly explanations that map model features and outcomes to domain concepts.
Expose explanations through a user-facing selection/presentation layer so stakeholders can retrieve context-aware, actionable insights tailored to their role.
impact: This approach increases trust, speeds troubleshooting, and enables domain-aware interpretation of models in manufacturing—making ML insights more actionable for engineers and managers.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: data → ML model → KG storage (features, outcomes, explanations) → LLM-driven explanation generator → user interface
Knowledge Graph schematic: nodes for assets, sensors, features, predictions and explanation links showing semantic relationships
Example explanation card: original prediction, feature contributions, KG context snippets, and a plain‑language LLM summary
Role-based view mockups: engineer vs. manager showing tailored explanation complexity and recommended actions
paper_title: Using Large Language Models and Knowledge Graphs to Improve the Interpretability of Machine Learning Models in Manufacturing
paper_authors: Thomas Bayer, Alexander Lohr, Sarah Weiß, Bernd Michelberger, Wolfram Höpken
